statement: Functions and arguments act together as declared, where that is a risk.
Precedence and overrides: where two settings say the same thing, the documented one wins.
An argument that changes another's meaning does so as documented.
Combinations that once had a bug stay fixed.
Scenarios: data to RTF, the file compared byte for byte.
as_rtftables(column_widths_twips = , auto_width = TRUE): the explicit twips win over the automatic widths.
plan_columns(widths = ) and plan_columns(column_widths_twips = ) in two calls stop at plan_apply(), asking for one of them.
rtf_tables() with several contents on a page: the page's section is the first content's with one; a later different one warns and adds no page.
rtf_tables() with several contents on a page: each title takes its own table's page values; the header and footer take the first table's, a later different value warns.
{AUTO_PAGE} in a source file stays a dynamic field after assemble_rtf(), so the assembled document numbers its own pages.
rtf_tables(auto_section = TRUE): a page that opens a section keeps the title carried on it (#728).
A later content on a page with its own font and colour has them declared in the document's tables (#730).
Headers and footers start in the document's font, then their own, so every reader shows them in it (#732).
A table from a data frame to an RTF file is written byte for byte as its reference.
A listing from records to an RTF file is written byte for byte as its reference.
A figure from a plot to an RTF file is written byte for byte as its reference.
Several contents on a page (a summary and its listing) to an RTF file are written byte for byte as their reference.
The plan verbs build a table's plan and run it into pages.
table_plan() starts a deferred, last-wins plan from the data and takes the roles: what goes across, what goes down, what carries the row identity.
plan_filter() drops the rows whose records fail a condition over the ARD's statistics and keys, judged across the columns.
plan_columns() declares the columns: widths by name, decimal alignment, row-title columns, auto width, the key separator, cell formatters and widths in twips.
plan_blanks() declares the blank rows: between groups, at the page edges, counted in the row budget, or between a listing's records.
plan_apply() runs a plan to its table, its RTF pages or a stage between (input, args, table, pages), the same way every time.
plan_layers() reads a plan from the outside: its roles, the layers merged by kind, and what its pages resolved to.
plan_template() writes the code of a plan from an ARD: both halves, the display half to be edited.
plan_header_tokens() lists the tokens a column header may carry ({col}, {n}, ...) with their values; plan_n_candidates() lists the populations a header's {n} can count.
plan_cells() says how each cell is made from the record's statistics: a token template per key (variable, context, kind, group, default), statistics as rows, and what an unfilled cell prints.
plan_digits() sets the digits of the open tokens by key or by statistic (and the rounding family), or formats a finished table's columns.
plan_levels() sets the order of a key's values (and a value's text); plan_labels() sets the text a value or a variable prints as.
plan_total() makes the ARD's overall rows a Total column (or a Total row), at the position given.
plan_stat_groups() groups a record's statistics into named groups that cols or rows name as .stat_group.
plan_compare() adds columns read from the ARD's comparison records (a test's p-value, a difference and its CI), placed on the variable's block.
plan_sort() orders the rows by keys or by a statistic, descending with a minus sign, keeping the groups together.
plan_nest() puts a variable's rows under one level of another variable.
plan_stub() folds the row keys and the label column into one stub column, indented by level, a group's summary on its heading row.
plan_col_header() writes the column header over the printed columns: rows, spanners and tokens such as {col} and {n} filled from the data.
plan_hide() keeps columns from printing while they still do their work (a page key, a sort carrier).
plan_cell_style() styles cells: the header, whole columns, or the rows a condition chooses; bold, italic, underline, alignment, colour, background, border, indent.
plan_style() sets the whole table's look: its border preset or rules by zone, the default look of header and body, widths, heights, padding, font.
plan_empty() writes a table of no events as one row saying so (and a footnote), when the table has no row or its overall row is 0.
plan_paginate_rows() paginates the rows within a row budget, keeping groups together as asked, with a continued label, inside BY pages.
plan_paginate_group() makes a page (and a section) per value of a column, named from a template.
plan_paginate_cols() cuts the columns into blocks of pages, carrying the kept columns, the header sliced per block.
plan_row_group() says what a run of rows sharing a value is and how the repeat shows.
plan_listing() makes a plan a listing of records: its printed columns (listing_col()) and the listing's layout.
plan_titles() and plan_footnotes() put a title block above and a footnote block below every page, or one block per page.
plan_after() runs the user's own functions over the finished pages, in order.
table_plan() returns a table_plan that holds the data unchanged with its roles and no layers, and computes nothing until plan_apply().
table_plan() classifies its source by the columns alone as normalized (.label/.kind), long (stat_name + stat, no context/groupN), ard (cards shape or not a data frame) or wide (anything else).

print() of a table_plan shows the source kind, the columns the roles may name, the layers in declaration order and whether plan_apply() gives a table data.frame or RTF pages (or says it has no layers).
table_plan(cols = c(KEY, ".stat_group")) accepts .stat_group as a role though it is not yet a column (plan_stat_groups() makes it at run time).
table_plan(cols = KEY) spreads one value column per value of KEY, the same table widen_ard(cols = KEY) gives.
table_plan(cols = c(K1, K2)) spreads one column per combination, named by the values joined with the key separator ("____" unless plan_columns(sep = )).
table_plan() with cols left out, on data with no group to spread, makes one value column named All.
table_plan(rows = c(name = KEY)) gives the finished table one row-key column per key under the given names.
table_plan() with rows left out uses the analysis variable as the row key, in a column named group.
table_plan(label = c(new = COL)) takes the row identity from COL (default ".label") into a column named new.
table_plan(label = NA) makes a table with no label column.
table_plan(label = list(row = c(A, B))) coalesces the columns, the first non-missing value winning per row.
table_plan(label = c(guard ~ "text", ~ "{.label}")) builds the label from a guarded template chain (e.g. NA .label -> "Total").
notes: checked only through plan_total() shift-table tests

statement: table_plan(stat = c(variable = , name = , value = )) names which of the frame's own columns play the analysis variable, the statistic name and its value.
table_plan(show_keys = KEY) puts a row key's own tabulation (rows marked .key_own) into the body as a block of its own.
table_plan(show_keys = NULL), the default, leaves a key's own counts out of the body (they feed only the header {n}).
table_plan() with a frame from normalize_ard() (including one edited between normalize_ard() and the plan) takes it as the input stage unchanged.
table_plan() with a long frame built without cards (keys, stat_name, stat) makes a table, plan-wide and per-variable digits included.
table_plan() with a finished (wide) table runs only the display half, giving the pages as_rtftables(read_meta = FALSE, ...) gives.
table_plan() with a frame of records and plan_listing() passes the rows through unnormalised and unspread, as as_rtftables(listing = listing_spec(...)).
table_plan(rows = c(soc = , pt = )) with a hierarchical normalized ARD and an overall row makes one row per SOC and PT, the overall row first.
table_plan(cols = KEY) with a factor KEY orders the value columns by the factor's levels.
notes: probe: reversed levels give reversed columns; no test asserts the order

statement: table_plan() with non-ASCII (Japanese) values keeps them unchanged as the value columns' names and the row keys' values.
table_plan() with a frame of zero rows stops at plan_apply(): "No cell was produced, so there is nothing to widen."
notes: message from widen_ard(); widen_ard test exists (test-ard-tables.R) but not through a plan

statement: table_plan() without x stops: "`x` (the data) is required."
table_plan(<raw cards ARD or a non-data-frame>) stops: "table_plan() takes the NORMALIZED frame, not a raw ARD"
notes: non-data-frame case (e.g. a list) is untested

statement: table_plan(<role> = <name not a column>) stops: "table_plan(<role> = ): no column '<name>' in the data."
notes: role shown as cols/rows/label or stat = c(variable|name|value

statement: table_plan(stat = <unnamed, unknown or repeated part names>) stops: "table_plan(stat = ) names the parts of a statistic your frame calls something else"
table_plan(stat = c(value = NA)) (a part not one non-empty string) stops: "table_plan(stat = ): each part is one column name."
table_plan(label = c(label = c(f1, f2))) stops: "table_plan(label = ): 'c(label = c(...))' is a named list of formulas"
table_plan() with cols left out on data that has a group stops at plan_apply(): "`cols` is required: the ARD has '<KEY>' to spread"
table_plan(show_keys = <a column key>) stops at plan_apply(): "`show_keys`: '<KEY>' is a column key; its own counts are the columns' populations"
table_plan(<finished table>) with no layers stops at plan_apply(): "This source has no statistics to read -- ... and the plan declares nothing."
notes: names plan_listing() and the display verbs

statement: table_plan(<finished table>, cols = ) or ARD-half verbs (plan_cells ...) stop at plan_apply(): "This source has no statistics to read -- ... but table_plan(cols = ) / plan_cells() need them."
plan_filter(p >= 0.05) drops the rows no column's record meets, giving the RTF of the same plan on a hand-filtered ARD.
plan_filter() keeps every value column even when all of a column's rows are dropped (columns are counted before filtering).
plan_filter() always keeps an overall row (normalize_ard(overall = ), e.g. "Any TEAE").
plan_filter() treats a record its statistics cannot answer (error or non-logical) as unknown, keeps a row no column answers, and reports it in the notes.
plan_filter() called twice uses only the last call's conditions (no combining).
plan_filter(cond1, cond2) keeps a record only when every condition holds.
plan_filter(n >= 3, TRTA != "Placebo") evaluates conditions over the record's keys as well as its statistics.
plan_filter(any = TRUE), the default, keeps a row when any column's record passes.
plan_filter(any = FALSE) keeps a row only when every answering column's record passes.
plan_filter(parents = "keep"), the default, keeps a parent row (a SOC) exactly when one of its children is kept.
plan_filter(parents = "drop") judges a parent row by its own counts.
plan_filter(by = KEY) makes the rows sharing KEY (and the keys outside it) in a column one record, each statistic read once, so a parameter's rows (n / mean / sd as rows) stay or go together.
plan_filter() with a hierarchical SOC/PT ARD filters PTs and keeps the SOCs they belong to.
plan_filter() that no body row passes leaves only the overall row, which plan_empty() then recognises as empty.
plan_filter(<no condition, or a named one such as keep = p > 0>) stops: "plan_filter() takes conditions, unnamed: `plan_filter(p >= 0.05)`."
plan_filter(any = NA) (not one TRUE/FALSE) stops: "plan_filter(any = ) is TRUE (any column) or FALSE (every column)."
plan_filter(parents = "x") stops: "'arg' should be one of "keep", "drop""
plan_filter(by = <a name that is no row key's column>) stops at plan_apply(): "plan_filter(by = \"<name>\"): not a row key.", listing the row keys by their column names.
plan_filter(<not a table_plan>) stops: "Expected a table_plan; pipe from table_plan(ard)."
plan_filter() on a finished (wide) table stops at plan_apply(): "This source has no statistics to read -- ... but table_plan(cols = ) / plan_cells() need them."
plan_columns(), even empty, makes plan_apply() run to RTF pages rather than stop at the table.
plan_columns() called twice merges field by field, the later value of a field winning and the others kept.
plan_columns(widths = <unnamed>) is col_rel_width, one a printed column in order (hidden and page_by keys not counted).
plan_columns(widths = <unnamed and shorter than the printed columns>) repeats its last value.
plan_columns(widths = c(col = w, .values = w)) sets widths by column name, .values covering every value column.

plan_columns(widths = <named>) naming no column of the table stops at plan_apply(): "plan_columns(widths = ) names '<name>', not a column of the table." with the printed columns; a hidden column's width is allowed.
plan_columns(decimal = ".values") aligns every value column at the decimal point, as set_decimal_split() on those columns.
plan_columns(decimal = c(<column names>)) aligns the named columns, following them by name.
plan_columns(decimal = <name not on the page>) ignores that name.
notes: probe: decimal = nope runs without a message

statement: plan_columns(row_title = <positions>) marks the row-heading columns, the positions counting printed columns.
plan_columns(row_title = c(<row key names>, ".values")) marks columns by name, .values for every value column.
plan_columns(auto_width = TRUE) passes as_rtftables(auto_width = TRUE).
notes: auto_width is not validated by the plan

statement: plan_columns(sep = s) is widen_ard(sep = s), the separator several cols keys are joined with.
plan_columns(sep = s) on an ARD plan is also the header_sep the spanning header is split on, unless plan_col_header(header_sep = ) says otherwise.
plan_columns() without sep joins column keys with "____" (e.g. Placebo____n).
plan_columns(cell_format = f or list(NULL, NULL, f)) passes as_rtftables(cell_format = ), same pages and RTF as the direct call.
plan_columns(column_widths_twips = w) passes rtftable(column_widths_twips = w), same pages and RTF as the direct call.
plan_columns(widths = , column_widths_twips = ) in one call stops: "plan_columns(): `widths` and `column_widths_twips` both set the columns' widths."
plan_columns() not called: no cell_format / column_widths_twips argument reaches as_rtftables().
plan_columns() on a finished (wide) table applies its settings to that table's pages.
plan_columns(widths / decimal / row_title by name) matches non-ASCII (Japanese) column names.
plan_columns(widths = <named, missing a printed column>) stops at plan_apply(): "The `columns` sheet gives widths, but not for: ..."
plan_columns(row_title = <position past the printed columns>) stops at plan_apply(): "plan_columns(row_title = 6): the table prints 5 columns (...); positions count those, or name the columns."
plan_columns(row_title = <hidden or unknown name>) stops at plan_apply(): "plan_columns(row_title = ): '<name>' is not a printed column: ..."
plan_columns(sep = <"", NA, several, non-character>) stops: "plan_columns(sep = ) is one non-empty string, "____" by default."
A column-key value containing the separator stops at plan_apply(): "'<KEY>' has a value containing the key separator "____" ('<value>')."
plan_columns(<not a table_plan>) stops: "Expected a table_plan; pipe from table_plan(ard)."
plan_blanks(), even empty, makes plan_apply() run to RTF pages rather than stop at the table.
plan_blanks(where = "between_groups") puts a blank row at each change of the first printed row key, never on the page key.
plan_blanks(first = TRUE) puts a blank row at the top of every page.
notes: first/last/counted are not validated (any value; isTRUE)

statement: plan_blanks(last = TRUE) puts a blank row at the bottom of every page.
plan_blanks(counted = TRUE) counts the blank rows in plan_paginate_rows(max_rows = ), as as_rtftables(count_blank_rows = TRUE).
plan_blanks(where = <row positions>) puts a blank row after those rows of each page.
plan_blanks(where = blank_rows_by_change() / blank_rows_by_rule() / a list of them) passes the spec to as_rtftables(blank_rows = ).
plan_blanks(where = "records") with plan_listing() puts a blank row after each record (listing_spec(blank_row = TRUE)).
plan_blanks() called twice merges field by field, the later value of a field winning.
plan_blanks(where = "between_groups") on a table with one group adds no blank row.
plan_blanks() on BY pages (page_by or plan_paginate_group()) applies between_groups, first and last within every page.
plan_blanks(where = "records") without plan_listing() stops at plan_apply(): "plan_blanks(where = "records") separates the records of a listing, and this plan has no plan_listing()."
plan_blanks(where = <an unknown string, e.g. "nope">) stops at plan_apply(): "Unrecognised `blank_rows` entry: nope" with "declared by: plan_blanks(where = "nope")".
notes: where = "none" is not a value: omit where for no blanks; from paginate.R

statement: plan_blanks(<not a table_plan>) stops: "Expected a table_plan; pipe from table_plan(ard)."
plan_blanks(where = "none") gives a listing's records no blank row between them (listing_spec(blank_row = FALSE)), and a table no blank rows.
table_plan() with a long frame (built without cards) of zero rows stops at plan_apply() with a message saying the table has no rows.
notes: a guard in plan_apply() before the long frame is prepared; the cards route (FR-PL124) gives the same message

statement: plan_template(ard, cols = ) prints and returns (invisibly, a character vector) the code of a table_plan() pipeline in both halves -- normalize_ard(), table_plan(cols = , rows = ), plan_cells() with the statistics the ARD has, then plan_stub(name = "row_label"), plan_row_group(mode = "indent"), plan_blanks("between_groups"), plan_paginate_rows(max_rows = 22, split = "group_safe"), plan_style(border = "tfl") -- and the code evaluates to a table_plan that runs to RTF pages.
The plan_stub() line is written without vars (derived at run time), and the display half is marked "edit this".

plan_col_header(values = list(n = TRUE), header = function(n) ...) is written only when pull_ard() finds one denominator per column and there is one cols key (its "\n" written as one backslash, R source); otherwise a comment explains and the pipeline still parses (the trailing pipe removed).

plan_template(cols = NULL) takes the ARD's first key and writes the NOTE "`cols` was not given; the first key is used."; keys outside cols become row keys (rows = c(SEX = "SEX", group = "variable")) with a NOTE naming them.
plan_template(hierarchy = c(SOC, PT)) writes normalize_ard(hierarchy = ), the overall label line when a sentinel is present (with a NOTE), and label = c(label = <the last level>).

plan_template(form = "widen") writes the immediate form -- normalize_ard() into widen_ard(), then as_rtftables() -- marked generated by plan_template(form = "widen"), with the keys outside cols as rows.
plan_template(file = ) also writes the code to that file, line for line.
plan_template(pipe = "|>") writes the base pipe; pipe = "%>%" writes magrittr's pipe and a library(magrittr) line.
plan_template(pipe = NULL) follows getOption("rtfreporter.ard_pipe"), then RStudio's preference, then "%>%"; another value stops: "`pipe` must be "%>%" (magrittr), "|>"".
plan_template(form = <other>) stops: "'arg' should be one of "plan", "widen"".

plan_stub(vars = , name = ) folds the named columns into one stub column named `name`, the heading rows inserted and the leaf rows indented: the pages as_rtftables(stub = stub_spec(vars, label = name)) gives on the same table.

plan_stub(vars = NULL) derives the stub: the row keys (table_plan(rows = )'s names; `group` when the rows were left to the analysis variable) and the label column, less the page keys (plan_paginate_group(), page_by) and the hidden columns.
plan_stub(name = ) is the folded column's name (stub_cols(label = )).
plan_stub(indent = n) passes stub_cols(indent = ): the indent of each deeper level.
plan_stub(group_summary = "all" / "none" / "empty" / "parent") passes stub_cols(group_summary = ): a leaf that is NA (or repeats its parent) folds its values onto the heading row.
plan_stub(before = FALSE), the default, folds the stub inside as_rtftables() after grouping and pagination (as_rtftables(stub = stub_spec(...))).
plan_stub(before = TRUE) folds it first with stub_cols(): the pages as_rtftables(stub_cols(tbl, ...)) gives, so a plan_cell_style() condition sees the printed rows.
plan_stub() with one column to fold (the label column alone) renames it `name` and folds nothing.
plan_stub() called twice merges field by field, the later value of a field winning and the others kept.
plan_stub() alone does not make plan_apply() run to pages: the plan still stops at the table data.frame until a display verb (plan_style(), plan_paginate_rows() ...) is declared.
notes: probe: .plan_reach() does not count the stub layer; the roxygen lists plan_stub() among the display verbs -- possibly unintended

statement: plan_stub() with none of the row keys / label column in the table stops at plan_apply(): "plan_stub(): nothing to fold." naming `vars = ` and the table's columns.
plan_cell_style() with the stub folded inside as_rtftables() (before = FALSE) stops at plan_apply(): "plan_cell_style() needs plan_stub(before = TRUE)."
plan_stub(<not a table_plan>) stops: "Expected a table_plan; pipe from table_plan(ard)."
plan_col_header(header = rtf_col_header(...)) sets the header on every page through set_col_header(); a row already as long as the table is left as written, positionally.
A header cell's {col} prints the column's name and {n} that column's number from `values`.
A header row shorter than the table has its last cell repeated over the value columns the spread produced.
With several cols keys {col} is the leaf (the last key's value) and {col1}, {col2}, ... the levels; the joined name ("Placebo____F") is never printed.
{n} in a spanner cell over several columns takes the single value given; {n:sum} totals over the columns the cell covers (a Total column left out); {n:<column>} names one column's value.
A {n} the data does not state prints NA, with one warning naming the cell and the reason ("printed as NA").
Pages split by a group value (plan_paginate_group()) each read their own {n} from the data rows carrying the page key.
plan_col_header(header = function(n)) (or function(n, tbl)) is called with the resolved values (and the finished table) and returns the header, so "(N=86)" is read, not written.

plan_col_header(header = <data frame of cells: line, cols, text, span, align, bold, border_top, border_bottom>) is resolved on each page: `cols` a column name, .values, a position, a range ("3:last") or "KEY = value"; `span` "each" (a cell a column), NA (one cell) or a key's name (a cell per value); plan_layers() reads it back as cells.
plan_col_header(lines = list(c(row_label = "", .values = "{col}"), ...), span = ) is the cells data frame written a row at a time: the same pages.
plan_col_header(values = TRUE / list(n = TRUE)) reads each column's population from the data -- a cards sentinel's N keyed by the cols, or the key's own tabulation -- at every depth of the keys.
plan_col_header(values = <a number, or a vector named by column key>) gives the numbers; one unnamed number fills every cell.
plan_col_header(values = list(n = "page", N = "table")) chooses the population on pages split by a group value, and a named list makes each name a token ({n}, {total}).
plan_col_header(values = <data frame>) is set_col_header(values = ): one row per page key (a `group` column), a column per {token}, each page filled with its row.
plan_col_header(header_sep = s) passes as_rtftables(header_sep = ): the separator a plain table's column names are split on into spanning rows; it wins over plan_columns(sep = ).
plan_col_header(col_header_align = ) passes rtftable(col_header_align = ), the same pages as the direct call.
A header given as cells whose text carries "{n" and no `values` reads the population as values = list(n = TRUE).
plan_col_header(), even with header_sep alone, makes plan_apply() run to pages; called twice the later header replaces the earlier (last wins per field).
plan_col_header(header = , lines = ) both stops: "plan_col_header(): give the header once, as `header` or as `lines`."
plan_col_header(lines = <not a list>) stops: "plan_col_header(lines = ) is a list, one element a header row"; span = <not a string> stops: "plan_col_header(span = ) is "each", "one" or a key's name."
plan_col_header(lines = list(c("x", "y"))) (a row not a named character vector) stops: "plan_col_header(lines = ): row 1 is a named character vector".
plan_col_header(lines = , span = <a list of another length>) stops: "plan_col_header(span = ) as a list has one element a header row; `lines` has 1, `span` 2."

A cells data frame naming a column, key or position the page has not stops at plan_apply(): "`col_header`: no column 'nope' on the page.", "'BAD' is not a column key; the keys are 'TRT'.", "`col_header`: position outside 1..5".
A cell's typed field of the wrong form stops: "`col_header$line` must be a whole number", "`col_header$bold` must be TRUE or FALSE" (yes/no/1/0 accepted).
plan_col_header(values = list(n = "bogus")) stops at plan_apply(): "a population is "page" (each page's own) or "table"".
plan_col_header(<not a table_plan>) stops: "Expected a table_plan; pipe from table_plan(ard)."
plan_hide("col") passes as_rtftables(drop_cols = ): the column is not printed; several names in one call or one character vector are the same.
A hidden column still does its work: a page_by key hidden still cuts and names the pages, and the positions of plan_columns() / plan_row_group() count the printed columns only.
Two plan_hide() calls add up (both columns hidden), and plan_paginate_group(keep = FALSE) adds its key too; hiding never un-hides.
plan_hide(<a name that is no column>) stops at plan_apply(): "`drop_cols` column 'nope' not found in the table." with "declared by: plan_hide("nope")".
plan_hide(<not a table_plan>) stops: "Expected a table_plan; pipe from table_plan(ard)."

An attribute given as a bare one-sided formula (bold = ~ is.na(group)) is evaluated row by row over the table's columns -- the folded row keys put back through rtf_stub_src, NA on a heading row -- and styles every column of the rows where its value says so; NA leaves the column default alone.
A named list of formulas (color = list(Placebo = ~ ...)) scopes each to a column by name.
The computed styles are built for the whole table and cut with the rows onto every page.
Formula styles are last-wins across layers (a later plan_cell_style() replaces the attribute); value styles (header / cols / where) run on the pages in the order written.
plan_cell_style(header = TRUE, bold / italic / underline / align / border = ) styles the column header as style_header().

plan_cell_style(cols = <names, .values for every value column>, bold / italic / underline / align / color / background / border / indent_twips = ) without `where` styles whole columns as style_cols(); cols left out, every column.
plan_cell_style(where = ~ <condition>, <value attributes>) styles the rows the condition holds for, over `cols` or every column (each attribute becomes ifelse(cond, value, NA) per row).
plan_cell_style() makes plan_apply() run to pages.
plan_cell_style() with no attribute stops: "plan_cell_style(): nothing to style -- give bold, italic, underline, align, indent_twips, color, background or border."
plan_cell_style(where = <not a one-sided formula>) stops: "plan_cell_style(where = ) is a one-sided formula over the table's columns".
A formula attribute with `where`, with `header = TRUE`, or beside a value attribute stops: "... so it takes neither `where` nor `header` ... Make it two calls."
plan_cell_style(header = TRUE, where = ) stops: "plan_cell_style(header = TRUE) styles the column header, which has no rows for `where` to choose."
plan_cell_style(header = TRUE, color / background / indent_twips = ) stops: "plan_cell_style(header = TRUE) takes bold, italic, underline, align and border."
plan_cell_style(where = , border = ) stops: "... a border is set on whole columns."
A formula list naming no printed column stops at plan_apply(): "plan_cell_style(bold): no printed column 'NOPE'." with the columns available.

A list entry that is not a one-sided formula stops at plan_apply(): "plan_cell_style(bold): each entry is a one-sided formula"; a value of the wrong type (bold = "yes") stops in style_cols() ("TRUE or FALSE").
A formula giving neither one value nor one per row stops at plan_apply(): "plan_cell_style(bold): the condition gave 2 values for N rows."
plan_cell_style(<not a table_plan>) stops: "Expected a table_plan; pipe from table_plan(ard)."
plan_style(), even empty, makes plan_apply() run to RTF pages rather than stop at the table.
plan_style(border = "tfl" / an rtf_table_border()) passes as_rtftables(border = ): the same pages as the direct call.
plan_style(border_header / border_spanning / border_body / border_first_row / border_last_row = rtf_border()) make one rtf_table_style() passed as as_rtftables(style = ).
plan_style(header_align, header_bold, header_italic, align, bold, italic, underline = ) are that rtf_table_style()'s look fields, in the one style object with the zones.
plan_style(table_width_twips / table_width_pct / table_width_pct_of_writable = ) pass by name, the same pages and RTF as the direct call.

plan_style(align_count_pct, font, font_size_half_points, row_height_twips, row_height_exact, header_row_height_twips, blank_row_height_twips, cell_padding_left_twips, cell_padding_right_twips, cell_valign, table_align, markup, blank_row_normalize = ) pass to as_rtftables() / rtftable() by name, the same pages as the direct call.
plan_style() called twice merges field by field (later wins, the others kept); not called, no style / width argument reaches as_rtftables().
plan_style(border = , border_<zone> = ) together stops: "plan_style(): `border` is the whole table's rules and `border_*` those of one kind of row. Say it one way".
plan_style(widths = ) or another per-column setting stops with R's "unused argument" (it is plan_columns()'s).
plan_style(<not a table_plan>) stops: "Expected a table_plan; pipe from table_plan(ard)."
plan_paginate_rows(max_rows = n, split = ) passes as_rtftables() the row budget and the split: the same pages as the direct call; it makes plan_apply() run to pages.

plan_paginate_rows(split = "group_safe") keeps whole groups together when they fit; "group_force" cuts at max_rows with the continuation label; "rows" cuts before `break_before`; "none" makes one page -- each as as_rtftables(split = ).
plan_paginate_rows(break_before = <positions>) with split = "rows" passes as_rtftables(split_rows = ).
plan_paginate_rows(min_group_rows = n) passes as_rtftables(min_group_rows = ).
plan_paginate_rows(cont_label = ) passes as_rtftables(cont_label = ).

plan_paginate_rows(page_by = KEY) passes as_rtftables(page_by = ): a page per value named by it, the row budget applied within each ("Period 1...1", "Period 1...2"), the same data and RTF as the direct call.
plan_paginate_rows(page_by = , heading = "Treatment: {value} (N={n})") names each BY page from the template: {value} the page's value, {n} its population from the key's own tabulation.
plan_paginate_rows(page_by = , heading_at = "section" / "title" / "none") is carried on every page as attr rtf_heading_at, the default of rtf_tables(auto_section = , auto_title = ).
plan_paginate_rows() called twice: the later value of a field wins and the others are kept (plan_apply(stage = "args")$rtf shows it).
heading = with {n} on a key whose population the data does not state names the page with N=NA and warns once: "the ARD states no population for 'A', 'B'".
plan_paginate_rows(heading = ) without exactly one page_by column stops: "plan_paginate_rows(heading = ) names the BY pages: give one `page_by` column."
plan_paginate_rows(heading_at = ) without page_by stops: "plan_paginate_rows(heading_at = ) says where the BY pages' names print: give `page_by`."
plan_paginate_rows(heading = <not one non-empty text>) stops: "plan_paginate_rows(heading = ) is one text with `{value}` and `{n}`".
plan_paginate_rows(heading_at = <other>) stops: "plan_paginate_rows(heading_at = ) is one of "section", "title", "none"."

plan_paginate_rows(max_rows = ) with split = "rows" / "none" (or with plan_paginate_group()'s "by_value") stops at plan_apply(): "plan_paginate_rows(max_rows = 4) has no effect with split = 'rows'." saying what to do.
plan_paginate_rows(page_by = <no column>) stops at plan_apply(): "`page_by` column 'nope' not found in the table." with "declared by: plan_paginate_rows(page_by = "nope")".
plan_paginate_rows(<not a table_plan>) stops: "Expected a table_plan; pipe from table_plan(ard)."
plan_paginate_group(col = KEY) makes a page per value of the column, named after it, handed to as_rtftables() as page_by (no split, no group_col) so the page key is never the row group.
The page name is the heading rtf_tables(auto_section = TRUE) opens a section on: one section per value, labelled with it.
plan_paginate_group(col = NULL) takes the outermost row key (table_plan(rows = )'s first name; `group` by default).
plan_paginate_group(keep = TRUE), the default, prints the key column; keep = FALSE adds it to drop_cols (hidden, the pages still cut on it).
plan_paginate_group(heading = "Treatment: {value} (N={n})") names each page from the template; {n} is the key's own tabulation (the .key_own rows), NA with a warning when the data states none.

plan_paginate_group(heading_at = "section" / "title" / "none") is carried on every page as attr rtf_heading_at, the default of rtf_tables(auto_section = , auto_title = ); NULL leaves the attribute off.
With plan_stub() the pages are cut by value before the stub is built (as_rtftables(split = "by_value", group_col = the page key)), and the page key is not folded into the stub.
plan_paginate_group() called twice merges field by field, the later value of a field winning.

plan_paginate_group(heading = <not one text>) stops: "plan_paginate_group(heading = ) is one text with `{value}` and `{n}`"; heading_at = <other> stops: "plan_paginate_group(heading_at = ) is one of "section", "title", "none"."

plan_paginate_group() with plan_paginate_rows(split = <not by_value>) stops at plan_apply(): "plan_paginate_group() splits the pages by the group value, and plan_paginate_rows(split = 'group_safe') splits them another way. Use one."
plan_paginate_group(col = ) and plan_row_group(group_col = ) naming different columns stops at plan_apply(): "plan_paginate_group() and plan_row_group() name different columns".
plan_paginate_group(<not a table_plan>) stops: "Expected a table_plan; pipe from table_plan(ard)."
plan_paginate_cols() cuts the columns into blocks of pages after the row pages, every block repeating the kept columns: the pages paginate_cols() gives on the same pages.
plan_paginate_cols(at = <positions or names>) cuts before those columns (paginate_cols(at = )).
plan_paginate_cols(cut_by = list(<blocks>)) is paginate_cols(cols = ); cut_by = <a separator string> is paginate_cols(by = ), with col_header = "names" the two-level header per block.
plan_paginate_cols(every = n) cuts a block every n columns a block does not keep, counted on the table as it turned out; a table no wider than one block is not cut.
plan_paginate_cols(keep = <columns>) is the columns every block repeats (paginate_cols(carry = )).
plan_paginate_cols(fit = TRUE) is paginate_cols(width = "fill"); fit = FALSE is width = "keep".
plan_paginate_cols(order = "across" / "down" / c("group", "rows", "cols")) is paginate_cols(page_order = ); allow_span_break = and col_header = pass by name.

The column cut runs last: plan_after() steps and the decimal alignment see the whole table, so a column position in them (set_decimal_split(cols = 4)) means that column, carried into the block that prints it.
More than one of at / cut_by / every stops: "plan_paginate_cols(): say where to cut one way -- `at`, `cut_by` or `every`."
plan_paginate_cols(fit = <not TRUE/FALSE>) stops: "plan_paginate_cols(fit = ) is TRUE (every block fills the sheet as page 1 does) or FALSE (each column keeps its width)."
plan_paginate_cols(every = <not a positive number>) stops at plan_apply(): "`every` is a positive number of columns."
plan_paginate_cols(<not a table_plan>) stops: "Expected a table_plan; pipe from table_plan(ard)."
plan_row_group(mode = "value" / "indent" / "filled" / "auto") is as_rtftables(group_by = ), how a group boundary is found: the same pages as the direct call.
plan_row_group(collapse = <positions counted on the printed columns, or names: the row keys, .values>) is as_rtftables(collapse_repeats = ): a repeated value printed once and then blank.
plan_row_group(group_col = ) on a plan of a finished table is as_rtftables(group_col = ), the column whose runs are the groups, the pages still cut by rows.
An ARD plan's groups are its outermost printed row key -- never a page key (plan_paginate_group(), page_by); folded into a stub, the stub's headings.

plan_row_group(group_col = ) on an ARD plan stops: "... This plan's groups are its outermost row key, table_plan(rows = ) -- name it there."; group_col = <not one name> stops: "plan_row_group(group_col = ) is one column name."
plan_row_group(collapse = <a name no printed column has>) stops at plan_apply(): "plan_row_group(collapse = ): 'grp9' is not a printed column".
plan_row_group(<not a table_plan>) stops: "Expected a table_plan; pipe from table_plan(ard)."

plan_listing(listing_col(...), ...) makes the plan a listing: the records pass through unnormalised and unspread, the pages as as_rtftables(x, listing = listing_spec(cols, ...)) gives; it makes plan_apply() run to pages.
plan_listing(...)'s listing_col()s are the printed columns, in that order, with their widths.
plan_listing(align = , record = ) are listing_spec()'s: the columns' default alignment, and the hidden record column (FALSE none, a string its name).
plan_listing(type, sep, spacer, spacer_rel_width, layout, wrap = ) are listing_spec()'s own, passed unchanged: the same pages as the direct call.
plan_listing() on a frame of zero records gives a page with no rows, not an error.
plan_listing(<not a table_plan>) stops: "Expected a table_plan; pipe from table_plan(ard)."

plan_titles(...)'s rows are the title block above the table on every page (attr rtf_titles) and plan_footnotes(...)'s the block below (rtf_footnotes); rtf_tables() writes them into the RTF; either makes plan_apply() run to pages.
plan_titles(pages = list(...)) / plan_footnotes(pages = ) give each page its own block, in page order.
Non-ASCII (Japanese) title text is kept as given on the page and written to the RTF as Unicode escapes.
plan_titles() (or plan_footnotes()) called twice: the later block replaces the earlier.

plan_titles(pages = ) with a count other than the pages' stops at plan_apply(): "plan_titles(pages = ) has 1 block for 2 pages." (and plan_footnotes() likewise), naming plan_paginate_rows() as what decides the count.
plan_titles("a", pages = list("b")) stops: "plan_titles(): give the rows of one block, or `pages = ` with one block per page. Not both."
plan_titles(<not a table_plan>) / plan_footnotes(<not a table_plan>) stop: "Expected a table_plan; pipe from table_plan(ard)."
plan_after(f, g) runs each function on the finished pages in order, each given the previous one's result (after the header, the decimal alignment and the cell styles).
plan_after() makes plan_apply() run to pages; called twice, both calls' steps run (steps add, they do not replace).
plan_after(<not a function>) stops: "plan_after() takes functions of the pages, one per step" naming plan_columns(decimal = ) and plan_paginate_cols() as the declarations.
plan_after(<not a table_plan>) stops: "Expected a table_plan; pipe from table_plan(ard)."

plan_paginate_group(heading_at = ) / plan_paginate_rows(page_by = , heading_at = ) is the default of rtf_tables(auto_section = , auto_title = ): the same RTF as saying it there; an auto_section / auto_title given to rtf_tables() wins.
plan_col_header(header_sep = ) wins over plan_columns(sep = ) as the separator the spanning header is split on.
plan_paginate_group() (a page per value) and plan_paginate_rows(split = <another split>) are not resolved by order: plan_apply() stops, "Use one."
plan_stub(before = ) changes what plan_cell_style() sees: before = TRUE folds first so a condition sees the printed rows; before = FALSE with a cell style is refused.
plan_paginate_cols() runs after plan_after(): a column position in a step (set_decimal_split(cols = 4)) means the whole table's column, not the first block's.

A hidden key (plan_hide(), page_by, plan_paginate_group(keep = FALSE)) shifts no position: widths, row_title, collapse and header cells count the printed columns, and a page key is never a row group (#635).
heading = "{value} (N={n})" on plan_paginate_group() and on plan_paginate_rows(page_by = ) reads {n} from the key's own tabulation bound into the ARD, never an analysis's N (#619).

plan_digits(n) plan-wide and plan_digits(<variable> = n) give the same table in either order: the variable's key formats its rows and the plan-wide default the rest; the same key written twice, the later wins.
plan_levels(KEY = ) and plan_sort("levels(KEY)") order the rows the same whichever is called first: the values plan_levels() names come first, in its order.
plan_paginate_rows() written twice: the later row budget cuts the pages (the pages the direct call with that budget gives), the split of the earlier call kept.
rtf_tables(titles = , footnotes = ) given with a plan's pages win over plan_titles() / plan_footnotes(); left out, the plan's blocks are the page's, in the RTF.

The page name auto_title adds (rtf_tables(auto_title = TRUE), or plan_paginate_group(heading_at = "title")) is the last row of the title block, after the rows plan_titles() gives; auto_title = FALSE leaves the plan's rows alone.

plan_paginate_rows(split = ) changes what max_rows does: "group_safe" moves a group that would cross the budget whole to the next page, "group_force" cuts it at the budget with the continuation label, "rows" / "none" refuse it.

plan_stub(before = TRUE) hands plan_paginate_rows(split = "group_safe") the folded rows, grouped under the stub's headings, so a page never opens with a leaf without its heading: the same pages as folding inside as_rtftables().

rtf_tables(auto_section = TRUE): a value's pages cut by the row budget ("Cohort A...1" opens the section, "Cohort A...2" continues it) and the next value's page each keep the title and footnote carried on them, and a section opens where the value changes (#728).

A later content's font and colours (page_break = FALSE) are added after the document's own, so the first content keeps its font and colour indices and its rows are written the same with or without the later content (#730).

rtf_footer() as rtf_header(): a band with no font of its own starts in the document's font (0, or the slots' default command when the document's font has slots), and a band with its own font starts in the document's then writes its own on its cells (#732).

plan_apply(stage = "auto"), the default, stops at the table data.frame when the plan declares nothing about the display and gives the RTF pages (a list of rtftable) when it carries a display verb (plan_columns(), plan_style(), plan_col_header(), plan_after() ...).

plan_apply(stage = "input") returns the frame going in: the data with the stat = roles' columns copied to variable / stat_name / stat, a coalesced label column added, and plan_total()'s overall rows relabelled; on a finished table or a listing the data itself.

plan_apply(stage = "args") runs nothing and returns list(widen = , rtf = ): $widen the widen_ard() arguments the layers resolve to (roles, cell options, the cells filled with the digits, levels, labels, sort, filter, compare, stat_groups, rounding), $rtf the as_rtftables() arguments (read_meta = FALSE, header_sep ...); on a finished table $widen is an empty list.

plan_apply(stage = "table") returns the table data.frame widen_ard() returns (with plan_nest() and plan_empty() applied) even when the plan carries display verbs; stage = "pages" runs the display half and returns the pages even when the plan declares nothing about the display.

plan_apply() on a plan with plan_listing() passes the records through: stage = "table" or "input" gives the records, "pages" or "auto" the listing pages; on a finished (wide) table "table" / "input" give the table and "pages" / "auto" its pages.
notes: stage = "args" on a listing gives the pages (not the args)

statement: plan_apply() remembers what each stage produced in the plan, so print() after a run names the columns after widen and as printed.
An error inside a stage names the verbs that declared it under "declared by:" (their own arguments, not the pipeline), and a role nobody declared is blamed on no verb (#507).
rtf_tables(doc, plan) renders the plan as rtf_tables(doc, plan_apply(plan, "pages")) does.
plan_apply(<not a table_plan>) stops: "Expected a table_plan; start from table_plan(ard)."
plan_apply(stage = "x") stops: "'arg' should be one of "auto", "input", "args", "table", "pages""

plan_layers() returns a list with data (the plan's data), roles, label (the label column's name), group_col, declared, layers, cells, compare, columns, header and pages (what plan_apply(stage = "pages") gives).

plan_layers()$declared is the kinds of layer in declaration order; $layers holds per kind the merged fields (a later layer winning; levels, labels and nest merged one key at a time; after and restyle one entry per call).
plan_layers()$columns gives names (the columns the pages print), spread (the value columns), page_names and widths (the col_rel_width plan_columns(widths = ) resolved to, NULL when none).

plan_layers()$cells parses each cell template (variable, context, entry with its labels and chains), NULL when the statistics are rows or no template is declared; $compare gives plan_compare()'s columns parsed with by and position, NULL without one.

plan_layers()$header has source "resolved" and the header as cell rows for a header the plan built (plan_col_header(header = rtf_col_header())), n_text the {n} scope ("page" / "table") as text or NULL, and literal_n TRUE when the numbers were written in.
plan_layers(<not a table_plan>) stops: "Expected a table_plan."

plan_header_tokens() returns a data frame token, kind, values (a list column), text, resolved, note, one row a token, and builds the table itself when the plan has not been run: {col} (kind "column") lists the leaf of every value column's name and, with several cols keys, {col1}, {col2}, ... each depth's values.

With plan_col_header(values = ), {n} (kind "population") lists each column's number, {n:sum} (kind "sum") their total and {n:<column>} (kind "one") each column's own; every named entry of a values list is a token of its own ({N}, {N:sum}).

A population the data cannot state (no variable / stat_name / stat for the columns, or no stated population size) is one row with resolved = FALSE, its text "-- NOT resolved: <reason>" and the reason in note.
print(plan) lists the same tokens and text under "header tokens".
{col} leaves out the row keys, the label column and plan_compare()'s columns, and includes plan_total()'s column; with the key's own tabulation in the data {n:Total} is the study total.
plan_header_tokens(<not a table_plan>) stops: "plan_header_tokens(): expected a table_plan."

plan_n_candidates() returns a data frame scope, page, column, value: a table not split by a group value has scope "all", one row per column key value the data states a population for, and one row (column NA) for the total over the columns; attribute differ is FALSE.

With pages split by a group value (plan_paginate_group()), plan_n_candidates() gives scope "page" rows per page value and scope "table" rows, attribute differ TRUE when a page's numbers and the table's are not the same, and page_col the column the pages are split on; the values are what the header prints with n = "page" / "table".
plan_n_candidates() on a plan with no cols, or whose data states no population, gives zero rows with the four columns, not an error.
plan_n_candidates(<not a table_plan>) stops: "plan_n_candidates(): expected a table_plan."
plan_cells("<template>") fills one cell per record from its statistics by the token template ({n}, {mean:.1f}), as widen_ard(cells = ) does; the keyed entries are passed as the cells map.

One unnamed entry is the plan-wide default; entries named by analysis variable, context, kind (continuous / categorical), stat group or default are picked by specificity, a variable's entry before its kind's before the default.

A named vector of templates (c("n" = "{n:.0f}", "Mean (SD)" = "{mean} ({sd})")) or cell_rows() makes one row per name, labelled by it; a guarded chain c(mean > 30 ~ "high", "{mean:.1f}") takes the first guard that holds over the record.
A later plan_cells() replaces an earlier entry for the same key and keeps the others (last wins per key).

plan_cells(stats = "cells"), the default, fills a template per cell; stats = "rows" makes each statistic a row of its own, labelled by its name, with the raw number in the cell (value = "stat", the default) or cards' formatted text (value = "stat_fmt", NA when the data has none).
plan_cells(na = ) is what fills a cell no template could (NA by default); on a finished table na alone is taken, as as_rtftables(na = ), and makes plan_apply() give pages.
plan_cells(notes = TRUE), the default, reports in a message the statistics no template used ("no template named it"); notes = FALSE says nothing, also when rtf_tables() runs the plan.
plan_cells(notes = FALSE) (or stats = , na = ) without a template adds no template layer: the resolved cells are the earlier call's.

plan_cells(<two unnamed entries>) stops: "Give at most one unnamed value (the plan-wide default); name the rest."; the same key twice in one call stops: "the same key is given twice in one call: 'a'."

plan_cells(stats = "x") stops: "'arg' should be one of "cells", "rows""; value = "x": "'arg' should be one of "stat", "stat_fmt""; notes = NA: "plan_cells(notes = ) is TRUE (report the statistics no template used) or FALSE."
A template carrying {x:%} with no plan_digits() for its key stops at plan_apply(): "`{mean:%}` asks the plan for its digits, but nothing declared them for 'default'."
plan_cells(<not a table_plan>) stops: "Expected a table_plan; pipe from table_plan(ard)."
A variable summarised under two contexts (summarised and tabulated) gets one entry per summary, each from its own key.

With plan_stat_groups(), a record of a split variable takes its variable's entry, else its group's, before its context or kind; a record that went whole to .others takes its variable's, then its context's or kind's, its group's after them.
plan_digits(n) fills every open token of every template ({mean} -> {mean:.nf}, {p:%} -> {p:.nf%}); a token that states its own digits ({mean:.4f}, {N:d}) keeps them.

A value named by statistic (c(mean = 1, sd = 3)) sets each statistic's digits; a statistic the narrower entry does not name falls through to the wider one; a value "4s" is 4 significant digits ({mean:.4s}).
Keys name an analysis variable, a context, a kind or default (plan_digits(1) |> plan_digits(AST = 3)): the narrower key wins for its variable and a later layer wins for the same key.
plan_digits(rounding = "r" / "sas") is the run's tie-breaking family (widen_ard(rounding = ): 2.125 to 2 dp is 2.12 / 2.13), last wins; plan_digits(rounding = ) alone adds no digits layer.

On a finished table plan_digits(<column> = n) formats that column with fmt_numeric() (n decimals, or "3s" significant), a later layer winning; plan_digits(.rows = c(<label> = n)) formats the value columns by the label column's text, also on a plan with plan_cells(stats = "rows").
On a plan with plan_cells(stats = "rows"), plan_digits(<column> = n) formats that column of the table of statistics, and a key that reaches no column stops as on a finished table.
notes: the column key is formatted when the pages are made, as on a finished table

statement: A key that reaches nothing stops at plan_apply(): "plan_digits() names 'nope', which matched nothing." followed by what a key may be (an analysis variable, a context, a kind, a column, .rows or default; on a finished table a column, .rows or default), so plan_digits(2) on a finished table stops naming 'default'.
plan_digits(.rows = ) on a table with no label column stops at plan_apply(): "plan_digits(.rows = ) is keyed by the value of the label column, and this table has none."
plan_digits(1, 2) stops: "Give at most one unnamed value (the plan-wide default); name the rest."; the same key twice in one call stops: "the same key is given twice in one call: 'a'."
plan_digits(rounding = "x") stops at plan_apply(): "`rounding` must be "r" (half to even, as base::round() does) or "sas" (half away from zero, as SAS ROUND() does)."
plan_digits(<not a table_plan>) stops: "Expected a table_plan; pipe from table_plan(ard)."

plan_levels(<column key> = c(...)) orders the value columns; plan_levels(<row key> = c(...)) orders a row key's values, named by the data's column or by the name table_plan(rows = ) gives it; plan_levels(<label column> = c(...)) orders the label rows.
plan_levels(variable = c(...)) orders the analysis variables (the blocks of rows); variables left out follow in the data's order.
A named element is a value and its text, as factor(levels, labels): plan_levels(TRT = c(B = "Drug", A = "Placebo")) orders B, A and prints them so; an element without a name prints as it is.

Layers merge one key at a time: a later plan_levels() adds a key without restating the others, and the same key restated is replaced; a map handed over whole (plan_levels(c(TRT = ...))) is its entries.

A value plan_levels() names that the data does not have makes no row and is said in a message (SEXC: "U"), whatever plan_cells(notes = ) says; a value present by its own name or as plan_labels() prints it is not said.

plan_levels(.drop_empty = <variables>) leaves out the levels of those variables whose n is 0 (or NA) in every column, a level some column counts staying, with or without an order; the default shows every level the data has.

plan_labels(KEY = c(value = "text")) prints a key's values as the text without ordering them, for a column key (the value columns' names) and a row key; a later plan_labels() for another key adds it, and for the same key replaces its entry.

plan_labels(variable = c(AST = "Aspartate")) or plan_labels(AST = "Aspartate") relabels an analysis variable's heading (its block), and plan_labels(SEX = c(F = "Female")) scoped by an analysis variable relabels its levels in the label column (#514); a scope naming no variable changes nothing, and a label sets no order.
With one analysis variable and no row keys, plan_levels(<variable> = c(...)) still orders the rows (#534).

plan_labels() names a value by itself or by the text plan_levels() gives it (plan_labels(SEX = c(Female = "Women")) after plan_levels(SEX = c(F = "Female"))); a text that is both a value and another value's text names the value, said in a message.
plan_levels(c("A", "B")) (an unnamed entry) stops: "plan_levels(): every entry is named by the column or variable it applies to,"; plan_labels() the same with its own name.
plan_levels(.drop_empty = 1) (not character, or NA) stops: "plan_levels(.drop_empty = ) takes variable names."
plan_levels(<not a table_plan>) and plan_labels(<not a table_plan>) stop: "Expected a table_plan; pipe from table_plan(ard)."

plan_total() makes the records with no value of the column key (the overall rows) one more value column, headed "Total" and placed last; without plan_total() those records make no column and are noted as unused.
plan_total(label = "All") names the column; position = "first" puts it before the key's values, also within the order plan_levels(<key> = ) gives.
The Total column's {n} is the study total the data states (the column key's own tabulation's N, or ..ard_total_n..), and {n:sum} leaves the Total column out.

plan_total(direction = "rows" / "both") adds a Total row per block from cards' plain margins (a key's tabulation without the body's variable), the corner from the row key's own, last or first by position; direction = "cols" (the default) writes no direction into the layer.

With two column keys the innermost is folded: each outer value gets a <value>____Total column from its records without the inner key; records with no outer key either make no column, and none at all stops: "no overall rows, rows without SEX".
Only the body's analyses are read: a comparison record (a test, plan_compare()'s) is no Total and leaves no empty row (#625).
plan_total() twice: the last call's label and position, its defaults included.
A factor column key keeps its levels' order with Total added last or first.
plan_total() on a plan without cols stops at plan_apply(): "plan_total(): a Total column is read for a column key; this table has no cols."
plan_total() on data with no overall rows stops at plan_apply(): "plan_total(): the ARD has no overall rows, rows without TRT."

plan_total(label = "Total") when the key already has that value stops at plan_apply(): "plan_total(label = "Total"): TRT already has a value "Total" (a Total made in the data?).  Keep one of the two."
plan_total(label = <not one non-empty string>) stops: "plan_total(label = ) is one text, the column's heading: "Total"."; position / direction outside their values stop with match.arg's message.

plan_total(direction = "rows") with no margins in the data stops at plan_apply(): "plan_total(direction = "rows"): the ARD has no margins -- a key's tabulation without the body's variable."; with two analysis variables in the body: "a Total row is the margin of one analysis variable; this table has 2".
plan_total(<not a table_plan>) stops: "Expected a table_plan; pipe from table_plan(ard)."

plan_stat_groups(N = "n", msd = c("mean", "sd")) gives each record's statistics the key .stat_group; with cols = c(KEY, ".stat_group") one record's groups are side by side as KEY____N, KEY____msd, and plan_cells() keys a template by the group's name; a statistic in no group is not read and is noted ("in no `stat_groups` group").
With rows = c(..., stat = ".stat_group") the groups go down, one row each, in the order their statistics first appear in the data; plan_levels(.stat_group = c(...)) orders them.
notes: the help says the order the groups are said; plan_levels(stat = ) orders too but notes the values as absent

statement: plan_stat_groups() twice: only the last call's groups apply.

plan_stat_groups(.variables = ) splits only those variables' records; the other variables' records go whole to the group .others names (every statistic with them, their own cell keys first), or are left out without .others.
The header's {n} of a group's column is its record's number (the arm's), and {n:sum} counts each record once (#709).
With cell_rows() one record lays out as n rows x m columns, across or down; a group with fewer rows leaves the rest empty, aligned row by row (#619).
The table and RTF are the ones a mutate() of variable before table_plan() gave (#619).
plan_stat_groups() with no group, or an unnamed one, stops: "`stat_groups`: every group has a name of its own (`n = "N", orr_ci = c("n", "estimate")`)."
A statistic in two groups stops: "`stat_groups`: 'n' is in two groups; a statistic is in one."; an empty group: "`stat_groups`: 'a' names no statistic."

plan_stat_groups(.variables = 1) stops: "`stat_groups`: `.variables` names the variables split into the groups: "RESP"."; .others not a group: "`stat_groups`: `.others` is one of the groups ('a'), where the other variables' records go whole."; .others without .variables: "`stat_groups`: `.others` needs `.variables` (which variables are split)."
plan_stat_groups(<not a table_plan>) stops: "Expected a table_plan; pipe from table_plan(ard)."

plan_compare(p = "{p.value:.3f}") adds a column p read from the comparison records (the column key with no value, in a context the body lacks), placed on the variable's block: the row of its label when the record has one, else the block's first row; nothing is computed.

Each named argument is a column, any name and as many as given; a template with guards (c(p.value < 0.001 ~ "<0.001", "{p.value:.3f}")); a named vector keyed by context (c(stats_t_test = ...)) reads that test only, a context no record has leaving the column NA.
cell_rows("1" = ..., "2" = ...) (or cell_rows("Mean (SD)" = ...)) puts each line on the block's row of that label, beside the body's lines.
plan_compare(position = "last"), the default, puts the columns after the value columns; "first" puts them before them, after the row keys and the label.
plan_compare(by = COL) makes one column per value of COL from the records carrying it, named by the value; with several columns in ... they are named <value>____<column>.
The comparison columns have no population: the header's {col} / {n} cells and plan_header_tokens()'s {col} leave them out, the header naming them itself (#631).
plan_compare() twice: only the last call's columns apply.
plan_sort("-estimate") orders the rows by a comparison's statistic as placed, in either call order (#684).
The RTF is the one a hand-made table with the same column gives (#625).
plan_compare() with no column, an unnamed one, or a name given twice stops: "plan_compare(): every column has a name of its own: `plan_compare(p = "{p.value:.3f}")`."
plan_compare(position = "mid") stops: "'arg' should be one of "last", "first""; by = <not one string>: "plan_compare(by = ) is one column, the key that splits the comparisons: "COMPARISON"."
A column named as a column of the table stops at plan_apply(): "plan_compare(): 'A' is a column of the table already."
plan_compare(by = "NOPE") naming no column of the records stops at plan_apply(): "plan_compare(by = "NOPE"): no such column in the comparison records."
Two comparison records of one variable reaching one cell stop at plan_apply(): "plan_compare(): two comparison records of 'AGE' reach the column 'p' on one row ... Split them with `by =`"
plan_compare(<not a table_plan>) stops: "Expected a table_plan; pipe from table_plan(ard)."
plan_sort(<keys>) on an ARD plan orders the rows as widen_ard(sort = ) and nothing reaches as_rtftables(); on a finished table it is as_rtftables(sort_by = ), with sort_desc from "-name".
A key is a row key or the label column by its output name, ascending; "-name" descending; a row key's empty value (a group's own row) comes first in its group either way.

A statistic's name totals it across the value columns ("-n": most frequent first); "<stat>[<col>]" reads one column ("-n[B]"); "max(<stat>)" / "min(<stat>)" the largest / smallest across the columns; "sum(n)" is "n".

"<stat>@<key>" carries the group's own row's value to every row of the group ("-n@soc": SOCs by their own count, each with its PTs); ".overall" puts the overall rows first and ".depth" a level's own row before the rows nested under it.
"levels(<key>)" puts the values plan_levels() names for that row key first, in its order, the others tying for the keys that follow.
Several keys, as several arguments or one vector, sort in turn: ties go to the keys that follow.
plan_sort(stat = "n") is widen_ard(sort_stat = ): a numeric .sort_stat column of the statistic's total across the columns is added to the table.
notes: the column is also printed on the pages unless hidden

statement: plan_sort(keep = FALSE) hides the sort keys that are columns of the table; a key that is not a column (a statistic, ".overall") is ignored rather than refused.
plan_sort(FALSE) keeps the rows in the data's order (nothing alphabetised); plan_sort(TRUE) clusters a plain key's equal values, first seen first.
plan_sort() twice: the last call's keys replace the earlier ones; plan_sort() alone does not make plan_apply() give pages.
A key that is neither a column nor a statistic stops at plan_apply(): "`sort`: 'nope' is neither a column of the result nor a statistic of this ARD." with the columns and the other forms allowed.

At plan_apply(): "-n[Z]" stops "`sort`: '-n[Z]' -- no spread column 'Z'."; "-n@zz": "`sort`: '-n@zz' -- 'zz' is not a row key."; "-zz@param": "`sort`: '-zz@param' -- 'zz' is not a statistic of this ARD."; "levels(zz)": "`sort`: 'levels(zz)' -- no row key 'zz'."
On a finished table a key that is no column stops at plan_apply(): "`sort_by` column 'zz' not found in the table."
plan_sort(<not a table_plan>) stops: "Expected a table_plan; pipe from table_plan(ard)."

plan_nest(CHILD = c(PARENT = "level")) moves CHILD's rows under PARENT's row of that level, into PARENT's group (the rows key carrying the variable), their labels indented by the stub's indent (4 non-breaking spaces; plan_stub(indent = ) the step), CHILD's own heading gone and the cells unchanged.
The level is matched as the table shows it, and a variable by its name or by its heading as plan_labels() gives it (variable = , its own key, or its own name among its levels).
The nested rows keep the order plan_levels() gives them and the text plan_labels() gives them.
A later plan_nest() for the same variable wins (plan_layers()$layers$nest shows it); another variable nests beside it.
A factor rows key stays a factor, its levels in the new order.

plan_nest() with no entry or an unnamed one stops: "plan_nest(): name the nested variable, e.g. plan_nest(RACESUB = c(RACE = "Asian"))."; an entry not one named string stops: "plan_nest(RSUB = ): one level of one variable, named by it: c(RACE = "Asian")."

At plan_apply(): a level the parent has no row of stops "plan_nest(RSUB = c(RACE = "Blue")): RACE has no row "Blue".  Its rows: White, Black."; a child with no rows: "plan_nest(NOPE = ): the table has no rows of NOPE.  Its group: RACE, RSUB."
A plan whose rows carry no variable stops at plan_apply(): "plan_nest() moves a variable's rows, and the rows carry no variable: name it on table_plan(rows = ), e.g. rows = c(group = "variable")."
plan_nest(<not a table_plan>) stops: "Expected a table_plan; pipe from table_plan(ard)."

plan_empty() on an empty table adds one row with text ("No subjects met the criteria.") in the label column (the row keys NA, the value cells ""), after the rows; a table that is not empty is as it was, with no row and no footnote.

plan_empty(when = "no_rows") is empty when no body row is left but the overall row (whatever its count); "overall_zero" when the overall row's n is 0 in every column (rows or not); "auto", the default, either.
plan_empty(position = "last"), the default, keeps the overall row's 0 above the sentence; "first" puts the sentence before the rows; "replace" leaves the sentence alone.

plan_empty(text = NULL) adds no row; footnote = adds that line to the pages' footnotes (after plan_footnotes()' lines) when the table is empty and makes plan_apply() give pages; a table that is not empty gets no footnote.
plan_empty() twice: the last call's settings, its defaults included.
A table whose body rows plan_filter() all dropped keeps its overall row and is empty (#691); with label = NA the sentence goes in the first column.

plan_empty(text = 1) or c("a", "b") stops: "plan_empty(text = ) is one string, or NULL for no row."; footnote = 1: "plan_empty(footnote = ) is the footnote's text, or NULL."; when / position outside their values stop with match.arg's message.
plan_empty(<not a table_plan>) stops: "Expected a table_plan; pipe from table_plan(ard)."
plan_labels()' text wins value by value over the text plan_levels(KEY = c(value = "text")) gives, whichever of the two is called first.
plan_cells(value = ) changes what a cell holds only with stats = "rows"; with templates the open {x} reads stat.
plan_digits() reaches only a token that left its digits open: {mean:.4f} beside {sd} keeps .4f while {sd} takes the plan's digits.
plan_sort() by a plan_compare() statistic gives the same rows whether plan_sort() or plan_compare() is called first (#684).
plan_total() with a comparison record in the ARD gives the table it gives without the record: a test is no Total (#625).
The header's {n} over a plan_stat_groups() column is the arm's number, each arm counted once in {n:sum} (#709).
With plan_compare() the header's {col} / {n} cells sit over the value columns and the comparison column keeps its own cell (#631).
plan_stat_groups() to an RTF file is byte for byte the file the mutate()-of-variable form gives (#619).
plan_total(direction = "both") to an RTF file is byte for byte the file the rewritten-margins form gives.
plan_compare() to an RTF file is byte for byte the file a hand-made table with the same column gives (#625).
plan_append() lays another plan's rows under a table's, the parts stacked before the pages are cut so that page groups are matched by value (#737).

A listing above its summary, written as two ordinary plans joined by plan_append(), gives byte for byte the RTF the same table built by hand gives: the time points across in two column blocks, the PK parameters across, the analytes across; the whole table's verbs written before or after plan_append() give the same bytes, and the later of two wins.

table_plan(value = ) makes a records plan: one row a `rows` key, the records' values spread across `cols`, one cell template, a template over the record as the row's text; it stops without `rows`, with `stat`, or with a value column the data has not.

A part's rows come under the parent's, the parts in the order declared, each under its name (part2, part3, ... or its own); a column a part has not prints that part's empty-cell text, which is each part's own; the digits are inherited from the parent key by key and the part's own win; a name given twice stops.

With plan_paginate_rows(page_by = ) the page groups of every part are matched by value: a page holds the parent's rows of a value, then each part's rows of it; a value the parent has and a part has not stops, or that part is left off the page with absent = "skip"; a value only a part has makes no rows; a part whose data lacks the page key stops.

plan_blanks(where = "between_parts") puts a blank row between the parts inside each page group, and a part's own plan_blanks(first = , last = ) a blank row above or below its rows; the blank rows are rows of the pages; between_parts on a plan with no part stops.

A part carrying one of the whole table's settings (the header, the columns, the pages, the column pages, blank rows between groups or parts, the style, titles, footnotes, the steps after, the column key's levels, another part) stops naming the verb and where it goes; a part with a different column key stops; something that is not a table_plan stops; a part may carry its own row verbs (cells, digits, labels, stub, a cell style with a condition, its own first / last blank row) and runs on its own.
The whole table's settings read the stack: the column header's {col}, plan_columns()' named widths and decimal split apply to the stacked table's columns.
